missionPremise: The 2026-09-11 ledger-as-serving-path ruling (`_decisions/2026-09-11_ledger_as_serving_path_seven_steps.md`, ADR-031 amendment) holds that the ledger is the serving path and a cell is accounting pointing at its atom. The operator's requirement, verbatim in substance per the dispatch: read the ledger, see every parcel, every one of its 65 facts, what serves, what has an atom. Nobody had measured how far the running system is from that as of 2026-09-16. This lane's job was to build the measuring instrument and run it -- not to close the gap it measures.
completionPredicate: A self-testing instrument (scripts/ledger-truth.mjs) exists, reused six-county-completeness.mjs's store-access pattern, passes 17/17 self-test including required not-vacuous checks, and its live output for both required probe parcels and the six-county rollup is captured in _inbox/ artifacts this close cites. All four pre-registered falsifiers are scored against live data, not asserted. A design-gap doc names what a cell must carry, what exists, which OPS-16 rows build the pieces (P-162/163/164/166/201/204), and states the tier-1-bake retire-or-feed question without resolving it (out of this lane's scope). This predicate is fully met. It is a DIFFERENT, narrower predicate than 'P-201 and P-204 are closed' -- this lane measured and reported; it did not build the verdict-enum split (P-201) or rule on any individual mid-cutover rail's disposition (P-204), both of which require code changes or an operator/lane decision this read-only lane was not scoped to make.
scopeBasis: Dispatch mission text is explicit: 'Read-only lane ... You spawn nothing. You write no product code and change no store. Your worktree is your dispatch planner's doc_repo worktree; write only under its _inbox/ and scripts/.' P-201 and P-204 are absorbed into this lane's plan-row list because this lane's measurement is their evidentiary input (P-204's own OPS-16 text: 'Depends on P-201, which is what makes this class distinguishable from P-203's' -- and this lane's own Mode 1 run reproduced P-204's premise parcel-for-parcel on the same gold parcel it was originally written against), not because this lane executes either row's own predicate. status=closed-partial reflects that split honestly: this lane's own deliverable is complete; the two absorbed rows remain open, owed to a build lane (P-201) and a decision lane (P-204).

This lane's Mode 1 setback-rule comparator (compareCellToAtom for setbackFrontFt/Side/Rear/Corner) reports 'n/a -- no single scalar to compare' rather than a real per-axis agreement check, because a setback-rule atom's body carries all four axes in one record while the ledger splits them into four separate rail cells. A real per-axis comparator is buildable (the body's front/side/rear/sideInteriorFt/sideCornerFt fields are visible in the raw atom body this lane already captured) but was left undone to keep this lane's own scope bounded to what its falsifiers required.
